context_for_next_testing_agent: Sprint v1.8.0 parity (sprint-header above grid + staggered fade-in + Copy all N Shorts + light-theme pills + per-variant copy + gated angle picker) all PASS. ONE REGRESSION to address: results-nav-collapse-toggle button in long-form mode is a no-op (handler fires but nothing collapses). Per-section header chevrons still work. The bug repros on history-loaded long-form scripts (and likely on fresh long-form generations too — same code path). Suspected root cause: vacuous-true `every([])` returning true when visibleSectionKeys is empty, OR a stale-closure issue where toggleCollapseAll captures an empty visibleSectionKeys before the memo updates. Fastest fix is a length guard at the top of toggleCollapseAll, or wrapping in useCallback. After fix: rerun the long-form history-open path, click results-nav-collapse-toggle, verify all 7 section-card elements gain .is-collapsed and the button text flips to 'Expand all'.
rca of the issue: results-nav-collapse-toggle no-op: handler `toggleCollapseAll` at Scripts.jsx:167 uses `visibleSectionKeys.every((k) => prev.has(k))` to decide whether to expand or collapse. When visibleSectionKeys is [] (vacuous truth), every() returns true and we always assign `new Set()`, so cards never get collapsed. Even when visibleSectionKeys is populated, if a stale closure from an earlier render is invoked (e.g., from a memoized child), the same empty-array vacuous-true bug fires. Reproduction: load /scripts, click a 'Long' history row, click 'Collapse all' button in sticky nav. Mitigation: add `if (visibleSectionKeys.length === 0) return;` guard at top of toggleCollapseAll OR change the condition to `visibleSectionKeys.length > 0 && visibleSectionKeys.every(...)` and wrap the handler in useCallback([visibleSectionKeys]).
